# Supplemental Data

## Supplemental Tables

### S.Table 1: CSV containing all variables used to assess weight contribution to new variable {#sec-s_table_1}
<button id="download-button2" class="btn btn-danger">
  <i class="fa fa-save"></i> Download S.Table 1B
</button>

<script>
  document.getElementById('download-button2').addEventListener('click', function() {
    const csvFilePath = './Figures/all_columns_list.csv';
    const link = document.createElement('a');
    link.href = csvFilePath;
    link.download = 'all_columns_list.csv';
    document.body.appendChild(link);
    link.click();
    document.body.removeChild(link);
  });
</script>

::: {layout-ncol=2}

![Figure S.2A: With balanced weights, our life expectancy model did a fairly good job at predicting life expectancy and did not appear to favor one group over another.](./Figures/conf_matrix_life_exp.png){group="conf_matrix_gallery"}

![S.Figure S.2B: As with our life expectancy model, binning our age-adjusted mortality rates allowed our model to balance both accuracy and fairness by not favoring one group over another.](./Figures/conf_matrix_mortality.png){group="conf_matrix_gallery"}
:::
